transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Nguyen (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Luca Romano (Redwood Solutions); Marta Diaz (Bluepeak Head of Search), Evan Cole (Bluepeak ML Eng), Sonia Patel (Bluepeak CTO)

[00:00] Jamie Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jamie from Redwood, and I'll hand it over to Priya for the technical part after a quick agenda. Um, just to confirm - are we all set with audio?
[00:06] Marta Diaz: Yep, we can hear you.
[00:08] Priya Shah: Great, thanks. So agenda: understand your current embeddings + rerank flow, what vector DB you're using, throughput/latency targets, and any constraints around private deployments or data controls.
[00:20] Sonia Patel: Sounds good. We're mainly interested in tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated - and whether private is feasible for us. We have regulatory customers so that might be needed down the line.
[00:30] Evan Cole: Quick background: we have a product search and a knowledge base search. Embeddings are generated nightly using a finetuned sentence-transformer, 768 dims. Index size is currently ~4M docs, about 3.2M vectors after filtering. Queries: median qps ~12, 95th ~60, burst to 200 during campaigns. Latency target for search+rerank is sub-200ms p50 and under 400ms p95 if possible.
[01:02] Priya Shah: Thanks, that's helpful. A couple clarifying questions: your rerank - is that a separate cross-encoder model that re-scores the top K retrieved candidates? And what K are you using?
[01:12] Evan Cole: Yes, we run a cross-encoder on top 50 candidates typically. The cross-encoder is relatively heavy - it's a 6B-ish model run on GPU for reranks in some cases; in other traffic we use a distilled model.
[01:26] Luca Romano: Got it. When you say 768 dims, are you seeing any quality plateauing if you try smaller dims? Have you explored product-specific quantization?
[01:34] Evan Cole: We tried 512 and saw a small drop for KB retrieval but not a huge one for product search. We haven't tried aggressive quantization in prod - mostly float32 for embedding generation then storing as float16 or PQ in the vector DB.
[01:48] Marta Diaz: Our main blockers are throughput and operational cost. The current vector DB runs on dedicated instances and is a big line item. We're evaluating alternatives that lower unit cost while keeping latency predictable.
[02:02] Priya Shah: Understood. On Redwood side we can run the embedding store and reranking pipeline in a few ways. Hosted API is simplest - we host embeddings and search, with Redwood-managed vector indexes and autoscaling. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU and consistent throughput and better isolation. Private (VPC/on-prem) provides full network isolation and KMS integration for keys. For your numbers - 3.2M vectors and peaks up to 200 qps with a cross-encoder rerank of top-50 - both hosted and dedicated are feasible with different tradeoffs.
[02:35] Sonia Patel: Can you run the rerank on the same hardware as the index? We're trying to avoid too much cross-service network cost.
[02:42] Priya Shah: Yes, you can colocate rerank workers with the retrieval nodes on Dedicated or Private deployments; for Hosted we'd usually spin GPU for rerank as separate callable endpoints but we have routing policies to keep latency low. Colocation on Dedicated yields lower inter-node latency and lower egress between services.
[02:59] Jamie Nguyen: Quick commercial note - we price hosted per-token for generation and per-vector for embeddings/search I/O; Dedicated is committed monthly capacity with a different unit economics model. We'll share detailed sheet after the call.
[03:12] Marta Diaz: Good. Back to vector DB: right now we're on Milvus using IVF-PQ for compressed storage. We do hybrid search - weighted blending of BM25 + dense retrieval - because product attributes still matter for recall. Integration complexity is a concern.
[03:30] Priya Shah: Hybrid search is common. Redwood supports hybrid scoring - you can do BM25 locally and then rerank by dense similarity, or use our integrated hybrid pipeline where you push sparse signals (like BM25 scores or filters) as metadata during retrieval. How are you currently doing reranking with BM25 signals?
[03:47] Evan Cole: We concat the BM25 score into the feature vector for the cross-encoder in the rerank stage. It's ad-hoc but works.
[03:54] Luca Romano: One pattern we've seen is using hybrid ANN for candidate gen and then feature-augmented reranker that consumes BM25, purchase recency, CTR features. That keeps candidate set small and the heavy cross-encoder cheap.
[04:06] Marta Diaz: That sounds aligned. Question on dimensionality and index size: if we drop to 512 or 384 dims, what's the expected index size savings and impact on throughput?
[04:17] Priya Shah: Rough rule of thumb: index storage ~ dims * num_vectors * bytes_per_dim. Using PQ or quantization can reduce storage by 4-8x. Lower dims reduces both storage and compute during nearest neighbor search. For latency, reducing dims helps but retrieval quality may drop; that's workload-dependent. We can help run an A/B benchmark comparing 768 vs 512 vs 384 on your data.
[04:39] Evan Cole: That would be ideal. We can provide a 10k sample dataset first.
[04:43] Jamie Nguyen: Great, we'll add that as an action.
[04:46] [05:00] Marta Diaz: On the security side: we need SOC 2, SSO (SAML), audit logs, and KMS integration. Any gotchas with hosted?
[05:10] Priya Shah: Hosted supports SOC 2 and SSO for the console/access. For customer-managed KMS and full network isolation you'd look at Private - Redwood Private supports VPC peering and HSM/KMS integrations. Dedicated sits in between: isolated capacity and tighter controls but keys are generally managed via integrations. We'll send the security pack.
[05:30] Sonia Patel: Data residency concerns - some of our customers require EU-only storage. Can Redwood host data regionally for hosted offering?
[05:38] Priya Shah: Yes, hosted has region options and you can pin data to EU regions; for strict residency and compliance, Private is the cleanest.
[05:47] Evan Cole: A couple more infra questions: for rerank, we rely on GPU for low-latency cross-encoder. What throughput can Redwood's serving runtime sustain for a 6B cross-encoder?
[05:58] Luca Romano: It depends on batch size and sequence length. For a 6B cross-encoder with 128 tokens input and batching, on an A100-class GPU you might get good qps when batching heavily, but tail latency is the issue. We typically recommend using a distilled reranker in-path for p95 latency-sensitive traffic, and reserve full cross-encoder for asynchronous or high-value flows. If you colocate and use multiple GPUs (Dedicated), you get better p95. We can run benchmarks with your model.
[06:28] Evan Cole: Understood. We are also evaluating moving to lower-dim embeddings to lower vector DB cost but want to ensure retrieval quality for KB. Are there recommended quantization profiles?
[06:40] Priya Shah: We have quantization profiles per model archetype - e.g., PQ-8 with 768 dims often gives good perf/space tradeoff; for very high quality KB retrieval we might recommend OPQ + residual quantization. We'll propose a profile after seeing sample embeddings.
[06:55] Marta Diaz: Integration: how do you sync vectors from our pipeline to Redwood? Do you push via API, S3, or do you host connector?
[07:04] Priya Shah: Multiple options. For Hosted, typical flows are incremental push via API or bulk load from S3/GCS. For Dedicated/Private, you can also run a data connector in your environment to stream updates. We support upserts, deletes, and bulk imports.
[07:18] Evan Cole: Latency budget for updates is nightly; we don't need near-real-time for most docs, but some product catalogs are updated hourly. Does Redwood support partial/streaming updates?
[07:28] Priya Shah: Yes, incremental updates are supported; for high-frequency updates we recommend a streaming pipeline with small batches to reduce index rebuild overhead.
[07:36] [08:00] Marta Diaz: Can you talk about fallback and graceful degradation? If the cross-encoder is overloaded, can you fall back to a cheaper reranker or cached scores?
[08:08] Luca Romano: Yes, Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallbacks - you can prioritize latency SLOs and fallback to a distilled model or cached embeddings. There's also an autoscaling policy for rerank workers; on Dedicated you can reserve burst capacity for campaign spikes.
[08:28] Evan Cole: Good. Do you have monitoring hooks for token/embedding costs and per-route latency?
[08:34] Priya Shah: Redwood Console has per-route metrics, token breakdowns, and tracing. You can set alerts on regressions for eval prompts too.
[08:43] Sonia Patel: About cost - can you ballpark hosted costs for 3.2M vectors with our qps profile?
[08:50] Jamie Nguyen: Ballpark only - rough estimate depends on storage tier and request rate. For 3.2M vectors with medium compression, storage could be in the mid-thousands/month and request cost scales with qps and rerank GPU usage. We'll provide a tailored estimate.
[09:06] Evan Cole: For the benchmark, can Redwood run both vector-only retrieval and retrieval+rerank with our cross-encoder?
[09:12] Priya Shah: Yes - we'll run candidate recall and end-to-end latency measuring p50/p95, and also evaluation on relevance metrics if you provide labeled data.
[09:22] Marta Diaz: We have a labeled holdout of ~2k queries with relevance labels. That should work.
[09:27] Priya Shah: Perfect. We'll use that to compare 768 vs 512 dims and different quantization.
[09:33] [10:00] Jamie Nguyen: Quick recap of next steps before we dig into a couple of more technical clarifications: 1) We'll send pricing and security docs, 2) SE to run benchmark with 10k sample and 2k labeled holdout, 3) schedule technical deep dive.
[09:52] Evan Cole: Sounds good.
[09:53] Priya Shah: Two technical clarifications: do you require exact nearest neighbor search for any flows, or is ANN acceptable?
[09:59] Evan Cole: ANN is acceptable; we use IVF-PQ today. We care more about recall for KB queries.
[10:06] Luca Romano: When you use IVF-PQ, we need to tune nprobe and PQ size; Redwood can help with a tuning sweep during the benchmark.
[10:15] Marta Diaz: Another question - for hybrid search, do you prefer merging BM25 candidates with ANN candidates, or use sparse-first pipeline?
[10:23] Priya Shah: Both patterns are supported. Merging candidates is simpler if you want to retain sparse signals; sparse-first can be more efficient if your sparse model has high recall for certain query types. We can test both approaches.
[10:33] Evan Cole: On ops - how are backups/restore handled for Dedicated? We need point-in-time restores and snapshots for our compliance.
[10:41] Priya Shah: Dedicated supports scheduled snapshots and point-in-time restore within your retention window; for Private you'd manage snapshots in your environment. We'll include snapshot/retention docs.
[10:53] [11:00] Sonia Patel: For Private deployment, what's the typical time-to-deploy? We have strict procurement windows.
[11:08] Jamie Nguyen: Private deployments usually take 6-8 weeks depending on approvals and access; Dedicated can be provisioned in 1-2 weeks after contract. Hosted is immediate for initial testing.
[11:18] Marta Diaz: That helps. A few nitty-gritty: can you support per-customer tenanting inside a single index or do you recommend separate indexes?
[11:26] Priya Shah: We recommend separate indexes for strong isolation, but multi-tenant metadata filtering works for logical isolation. Depends on compliance needs.
[11:35] Evan Cole: Any limitations on dimensionality? Our pipeline could move to 1024 dims if needed.
[11:42] Luca Romano: Supported - larger dims increase storage and compute but are fine with the right quantization and Dedicated capacity. We'll include performance notes.
[11:50] [12:00] Marta Diaz: Are there known gotchas when migrating from Milvus to Redwood-managed indexes?
[12:00] Priya Shah: The main ones: index param tuning (IVF/PQ params differ), data format for metadata, and incremental update flow. We have migration guides and tooling to bulk-import Milvus dumps. Some index settings need retuning for Redwood runtime.
[12:16] Evan Cole: Great. For the benchmarking timeline - what do you need from us to get started this week?
[12:22] Priya Shah: We'll need 10k sample vectors + the 2k labeled holdout, a short doc describing your generation pipeline and any filters, and SSH/placeholder creds for an S3 bucket or a temporary upload. Also an estimation of the cross-encoder model checkpoint (we need weights or a container to run it).
[12:38] Javier? [transcription artifact]: Sorry, I think misattributed - ignore.
[12:40] Jamie Nguyen: Noted - we'll get that started.
[12:42] Marta Diaz: One last question on observability: can we trace requests from query reception through retrieval and rerank with per-request tracing ids?
[12:50] Priya Shah: Yes, Redwood tracing enables per-request traces and you can correlate with logs and console metrics. We'll provide examples.
[12:58] Sonia Patel: Anything else on your side?
[13:00] Jamie Nguyen: No, just next steps. We'll follow up with the pricing and security pack later today.
[13:04] Priya Shah: SE will send the benchmark plan and sample ingestion steps.
[13:08] Evan Cole: Thanks all. Looking forward to the benchmark.
[13:12] Marta Diaz: Thanks.
[13:14] Jamie Nguyen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker labels occasionally generic; brief misattribution at ~12:38. Some technical terms transcribed loosely (OPQ, PQ, IVF).

Benchmarks proposed:
- 10k sample ingestion test: compare 768/512/384 dims, PQ-8 vs PQ-16, measure recall@10 and p50/p95 latency for retrieval-only and retrieval+rerank.
- End-to-end run with cross-encoder on Redwood hosted to measure GPU cost and latency.

References mentioned:
- Milvus (current vector DB)
- IVF-PQ indexing
- BM25 + dense hybrid search
- SOC 2, SAML, KMS, VPC peering
